passages.text: That same day King Xerxes awarded Queen Esther the estate of Haman, the enemy of the Jews. And Mordecai entered the king’s presence because Esther had revealed his relation to her.
passages.sermon:
King Xerxes ruled the Persian Empire.
Queen Esther was his wife.
Haman was the enemy of the Jews.
On that same day, King Xerxes gave Queen Esther the estate of Haman.
Mordecai was related to Esther.
Esther told the king about her relation to Mordecai.
Because of this, Mordecai came before the king.
passages.original: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא נָתַ֞ן הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ֙ לְאֶסְתֵּ֣ר הַמַּלְכָּ֔ה אֶת־ בֵּ֥ית הָמָ֖ן צֹרֵ֣ר הַיְּהוּדִיִּים וּמָרְדֳּכַ֗י בָּ֚א לִפְנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ כִּֽי־ הִגִּ֥ידָה אֶסְתֵּ֖ר מַ֥ה הוּא־ לָֽהּ׃

passages.text: The king removed the signet ring he had recovered from Haman and presented it to Mordecai. And Esther appointed Mordecai over the estate of Haman.
passages.sermon:
King Ahasuerus took his signet ring.
He had taken this ring from Haman.
King Ahasuerus gave the ring to Mordecai.
Esther was the queen.
Esther put Mordecai in charge of Haman’s estate.
passages.original: וַיָּ֨סַר הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ אֶת־ טַבַּעְתּ֗וֹ אֲשֶׁ֤ר הֶֽעֱבִיר֙ מֵֽהָמָ֔ן וַֽיִּתְּנָ֖הּ לְמָרְדֳּכָ֑י וַתָּ֧שֶׂם אֶסְתֵּ֛ר אֶֽת־ מָרְדֳּכַ֖י עַל־ בֵּ֥ית הָמָֽן׃פ

passages.text: And once again, Esther addressed the king. She fell at his feet weeping and begged him to revoke the evil scheme of Haman the Agagite, which he had devised against the Jews.
passages.sermon:
Esther was the queen.
Esther spoke to the king again.
She fell at the king’s feet.
She wept.
She begged the king.
She asked him to remove the evil plan of Haman the Agagite.
Haman had planned evil against the Jews.
passages.original: וַתּ֣וֹסֶף אֶסְתֵּ֗ר וַתְּדַבֵּר֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַתִּפֹּ֖ל לִפְנֵ֣י רַגְלָ֑יו וַתֵּ֣בְךְּ וַתִּתְחַנֶּן־ ל֗וֹ לְהַֽעֲבִיר֙ אֶת־ רָעַת֙ הָמָ֣ן הָֽאֲגָגִ֔י וְאֵת֙ מַֽחֲשַׁבְתּ֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר חָשַׁ֖ב עַל־ הַיְּהוּדִֽים׃

passages.text: The king extended the gold scepter toward Esther, and she arose and stood before the king.
passages.sermon:
King Xerxes sat on his throne.
He saw Esther.
He extended his gold scepter toward Esther.
Esther saw the king’s gold scepter.
Esther stood up.
Esther stood before King Xerxes.
passages.original: וַיּ֤וֹשֶׁט הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ לְאֶסְתֵּ֔ר אֵ֖ת שַׁרְבִ֣ט הַזָּהָ֑ב וַתָּ֣קָם אֶסְתֵּ֔ר וַֽתַּעֲמֹ֖ד לִפְנֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: “If it pleases the king,” she said, “and if I have found favor in his sight, and the matter seems proper to the king, and I am pleasing in his sight, may an order be written to revoke the letters that the scheming Haman son of Hammedatha, the Agagite, wrote to destroy the Jews in all the king’s provinces.
passages.sermon:
Esther spoke to the king.
Esther was the queen.
She said, “If it pleases the king, let me speak.”
She said, “If I have found favor in the king’s sight, listen to my request.”
She said, “If the matter seems right to the king, and if I am pleasing to him, please act.”
She asked the king to write an order.
She asked the king to revoke the letters written by Haman.
Haman was the son of Hammedatha.
Haman was an Agagite.
Haman wrote letters to destroy the Jews.
These Jews lived in all the provinces of the king.
Esther asked the king to cancel Haman’s evil plan.
passages.original: וַ֠תֹּאמֶר אִם־ עַל־ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ ט֜וֹב וְאִם־ מָצָ֧אתִי חֵ֣ן לְפָנָ֗יו וְכָשֵׁ֤ר הַדָּבָר֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְטוֹבָ֥ה אֲנִ֖י בְּעֵינָ֑יו יִכָּתֵ֞ב לְהָשִׁ֣יב אֶת־ הַסְּפָרִ֗ים מַחֲשֶׁ֜בֶת הָמָ֤ן בֶּֽן־ הַמְּדָ֙תָא֙ הָאֲגָגִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֣ר כָּתַ֗ב לְאַבֵּד֙ אֶת־ הַיְּהוּדִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּכָל־ מְדִינ֥וֹת הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: For how could I bear to see the disaster that would befall my people? How could I bear to see the destruction of my kindred?”
passages.sermon:
Esther was a Jewish queen of Persia.
She spoke to King Xerxes.
Esther cared deeply for her people, the Jews.
She said, “I cannot bear to see disaster come upon my people.”
She also said, “I cannot bear to see the destruction of my family.”
passages.original: כִּ֠י אֵיכָכָ֤ה אוּכַל֙ וְֽרָאִ֔יתִי בָּרָעָ֖ה אֲשֶׁר־ יִמְצָ֣א אֶת־ עַמִּ֑י וְאֵֽיכָכָ֤ה אוּכַל֙ וְֽרָאִ֔יתִי בְּאָבְדַ֖ן מוֹלַדְתִּֽי׃ס

passages.text: So King Xerxes said to Esther the Queen and Mordecai the Jew, “Behold, I have given Haman’s estate to Esther, and he was hanged on the gallows because he attacked the Jews.
passages.sermon:
King Xerxes was the ruler of the Persian Empire.
Esther was the queen.
Mordecai was a Jew.
King Xerxes spoke to Esther and Mordecai.
He said, “I have given Haman’s estate to Esther.
Haman was hanged on the gallows.
He was punished because he attacked the Jews.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵרֹשׁ֙ לְאֶסְתֵּ֣ר הַמַּלְכָּ֔ה וּֽלְמָרְדֳּכַ֖י הַיְּהוּדִ֑י הִנֵּ֨ה בֵית־ הָמָ֜ן נָתַ֣תִּי לְאֶסְתֵּ֗ר וְאֹתוֹ֙ תָּל֣וּ עַל־ הָעֵ֔ץ עַ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־ שָׁלַ֥ח יָד֖וֹ בַּיְּהוּדִיִּים׃

passages.text: Now you may write in the king’s name as you please regarding the Jews, and seal it with the royal signet ring. For a decree that is written in the name of the king and sealed with the royal signet ring cannot be revoked.”
passages.sermon:
King Xerxes spoke to Esther and Mordecai.
He gave them authority over matters concerning the Jews.
He said, “You may write about the Jews as you see fit.
Write in the name of the king.
Seal the letter with the king’s signet ring.
A decree written in the king’s name cannot be changed.
A decree sealed with the king’s signet ring cannot be revoked.”
passages.original: וְ֠אַתֶּם כִּתְב֨וּ עַל־ הַיְּהוּדִ֜ים כַּטּ֤וֹב בְּעֵֽינֵיכֶם֙ בְּשֵׁ֣ם הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְחִתְמ֖וּ בְּטַבַּ֣עַת הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ כִּֽי־ כְתָ֞ב אֲשֶׁר־ נִכְתָּ֣ב בְּשֵׁם־ הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ וְנַחְתּ֛וֹם בְּטַבַּ֥עַת הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֵ֥ין לְהָשִֽׁיב׃

passages.text: At once the royal scribes were summoned, and on the twenty-third day of the third month (the month of Sivan ), they recorded all of Mordecai’s orders to the Jews and to the satraps, governors, and princes of the 127 provinces from India to Cush —writing to each province in its own script, to every people in their own language, and to the Jews in their own script and language.
passages.sermon:
The royal scribes served King Xerxes.
They were summoned immediately.
This happened at that time.
It was the third month.
The third month is called Sivan.
It was the twenty-third day of Sivan.
The scribes wrote down everything Mordecai commanded.
Mordecai gave orders to the Jews.
He also gave orders to the satraps, governors, and princes.
These officials ruled the provinces.
There were 127 provinces.
The provinces stretched from India to Cush.
The scribes wrote to each province in its own script.
They wrote to every people in their own language.
They wrote to the Jews in their own script and language.
passages.original: וַיִּקָּרְא֣וּ סֹפְרֵֽי־ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ בָּֽעֵת־ הַ֠הִיא בַּחֹ֨דֶשׁ הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֜י הוּא־ חֹ֣דֶשׁ סִיוָ֗ן בִּשְׁלוֹשָׁ֣ה וְעֶשְׂרִים֮ בּוֹ֒ וַיִּכָּתֵ֣ב כְּֽכָל־ אֲשֶׁר־ צִוָּ֣ה מָרְדֳּכַ֣י אֶל־ הַיְּהוּדִ֡ים וְאֶ֣ל הָאֲחַשְׁדַּרְפְּנִֽים־ וְהַפַּחוֹת֩ וְשָׂרֵ֨י הַמְּדִינ֜וֹת אֲשֶׁ֣ר׀ מֵהֹ֣דּוּ וְעַד־ כּ֗וּשׁ שֶׁ֣בַע וְעֶשְׂרִ֤ים וּמֵאָה֙ מְדִינָ֔ה מְדִינָ֤ה וּמְדִינָה֙ כִּכְתָבָ֔הּ וְעַ֥ם וָעָ֖ם כִּלְשֹׁנ֑וֹ וְאֶ֨ל־ הַיְּהוּדִ֔ים כִּכְתָבָ֖ם וְכִלְשׁוֹנָֽם׃

passages.text: Mordecai wrote in the name of King Xerxes and sealed it with the royal signet ring. He sent the documents by mounted couriers riding on swift horses bred from the royal mares.
passages.sermon:
Mordecai acted with the king’s authority.
He wrote in the name of King Xerxes.
He sealed the writing with the king’s royal signet ring.
Mordecai sent the documents to others.
He gave the documents to mounted couriers.
The couriers rode on swift horses.
These horses were bred from the royal mares.
passages.original: וַיִּכְתֹּ֗ב בְּשֵׁם֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵרֹ֔שׁ וַיַּחְתֹּ֖ם בְּטַבַּ֣עַת הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח סְפָרִ֡ים בְּיַד֩ הָרָצִ֨ים בַּסּוּסִ֜ים רֹכְבֵ֤י הָרֶ֙כֶשׁ֙ הָֽאֲחַשְׁתְּרָנִ֔ים בְּנֵ֖י הָֽרַמָּכִֽים׃

passages.text: By these letters the king permitted the Jews in each and every city the right to assemble and defend themselves, to destroy, kill, and annihilate all the forces of any people or province hostile to them, including women and children, and to plunder their possessions.
passages.sermon:
King Xerxes gave the Jews a new right.
The Jews lived in every city of his kingdom.
The king allowed the Jews to gather together.
He allowed them to defend themselves.
The Jews could destroy anyone who attacked them.
They could kill anyone who was their enemy.
They could wipe out all the forces of any people or province that opposed them.
This included men, women, and children who were hostile to the Jews.
The Jews could also take the possessions of their enemies.
passages.original: אֲשֶׁר֩ נָתַ֨ן הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ לַיְּהוּדִ֣ים׀ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּכָל־ עִיר־ וָעִ֗יר לְהִקָּהֵל֮ וְלַעֲמֹ֣ד עַל־ נַפְשָׁם֒ לְהַשְׁמִיד֩ וְלַהֲרֹ֨ג וּלְאַבֵּ֜ד אֶת־ כָּל־ חֵ֨יל עַ֧ם וּמְדִינָ֛ה הַצָּרִ֥ים אֹתָ֖ם טַ֣ף וְנָשִׁ֑ים וּשְׁלָלָ֖ם לָבֽוֹז׃

passages.text: The single day appointed throughout all the provinces of King Xerxes was the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, the month of Adar.
passages.sermon:
King Xerxes ruled many provinces.
He appointed a single day for an important event.
This day was the thirteenth day of the twelfth month.
The twelfth month is called Adar.
This command applied to every province under King Xerxes.
passages.original: בְּי֣וֹם אֶחָ֔ד בְּכָל־ מְדִינ֖וֹת הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵר֑וֹשׁ בִּשְׁלוֹשָׁ֥ה עָשָׂ֛ר לְחֹ֥דֶשׁ שְׁנֵים־ עָשָׂ֖ר הוּא־ חֹ֥דֶשׁ אֲדָֽר׃

passages.text: A copy of the text of the edict was to be issued in every province and published to all the people, so that the Jews would be ready on that day to avenge themselves on their enemies.
passages.sermon:
The king issued an edict.
The king ruled over many provinces.
Officials made a copy of the edict.
They sent the copy to every province.
They published the edict to all the people.
Everyone could see and understand the command.
The Jews lived in these provinces.
The Jews needed to be ready for a special day.
On that day, the Jews could take action against their enemies.
The Jews could avenge themselves on those who hated them.
passages.original: פַּתְשֶׁ֣גֶן הַכְּתָ֗ב לְהִנָּ֤תֵֽן דָּת֙ בְּכָל־ מְדִינָ֣ה וּמְדִינָ֔ה גָּל֖וּי לְכָל־ הָעַמִּ֑ים וְלִהְי֨וֹת הַיְּהוּדִיִּים עֲתוּדִים לַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה לְהִנָּקֵ֖ם מֵאֹיְבֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: The couriers rode out in haste on their royal horses, pressed on by the command of the king. And the edict was also issued in the citadel of Susa.
passages.sermon:
The couriers rode royal horses.
The couriers left quickly.
The king commanded them to hurry.
The king’s edict was given in Susa.
Susa was the royal citadel.
passages.original: הָרָצִ֞ים רֹכְבֵ֤י הָרֶ֙כֶשׁ֙ הָֽאֲחַשְׁתְּרָנִ֔ים יָֽצְא֛וּ מְבֹהָלִ֥ים וּדְחוּפִ֖ים בִּדְבַ֣ר הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וְהַדָּ֥ת נִתְּנָ֖ה בְּשׁוּשַׁ֥ן הַבִּירָֽה׃פ

passages.text: Mordecai went out from the presence of the king in royal garments of blue and white, with a large gold crown and a purple robe of fine linen. And the city of Susa shouted and rejoiced.
passages.sermon:
Mordecai was a Jew.
Mordecai had just been with the king.
Mordecai left the king’s presence.
Mordecai wore royal garments.
His garments were blue and white.
Mordecai wore a large gold crown.
He also wore a purple robe made of fine linen.
The city of Susa saw Mordecai.
The people of Susa shouted.
The people of Susa rejoiced.
passages.original: וּמָרְדֳּכַ֞י יָצָ֣א׀ מִלִּפְנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ בִּלְב֤וּשׁ מַלְכוּת֙ תְּכֵ֣לֶת וָח֔וּר וַעֲטֶ֤רֶת זָהָב֙ גְּדוֹלָ֔ה וְתַכְרִ֥יךְ בּ֖וּץ וְאַרְגָּמָ֑ן וְהָעִ֣יר שׁוּשָׁ֔ן צָהֲלָ֖ה וְשָׂמֵֽחָה׃

passages.text: For the Jews it was a time of light and gladness, of joy and honor.
passages.sermon:
The Jews had light.
The Jews had gladness.
The Jews had joy.
The Jews had honor.
passages.original: לַיְּהוּדִ֕ים הָֽיְתָ֥ה אוֹרָ֖ה וְשִׂמְחָ֑ה וְשָׂשֹׂ֖ן וִיקָֽר׃

passages.text: In every province and every city, wherever the king’s edict and decree reached, there was joy and gladness among the Jews, with feasting and celebrating. And many of the people of the land themselves became Jews, because the fear of the Jews had fallen upon them.
passages.sermon:
The king sent out an edict and a decree.
This message reached every province and every city.
The Jews lived in these places.
The Jews heard the king’s command.
The Jews felt joy and gladness.
The Jews held feasts.
The Jews celebrated with good days.
Many people of the land saw this.
Many people of the land became Jews.
These people feared the Jews.
The fear of the Jews had fallen upon them.
passages.original: וּבְכָל־ מְדִינָ֨ה וּמְדִינָ֜ה וּבְכָל־ עִ֣יר וָעִ֗יר מְקוֹם֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר דְּבַר־ הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ וְדָתוֹ֙ מַגִּ֔יעַ שִׂמְחָ֤ה וְשָׂשׂוֹן֙ לַיְּהוּדִ֔ים מִשְׁתֶּ֖ה וְי֣וֹם ט֑וֹב וְרַבִּ֞ים מֵֽעַמֵּ֤י הָאָ֙רֶץ֙ מִֽתְיַהֲדִ֔ים כִּֽי־ נָפַ֥ל פַּֽחַד־ הַיְּהוּדִ֖ים עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃
